skill.name: code-reviewer
skill.description: Guides AI assistants through structured code reviews for quality, security, performance, testing, and documentation.
skill.summary: Structured code review guidance for quality, security, performance, testing, and documentation.
skill.author: DennisLiuCk

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives. The flagged lines are Markdown examples that show unsafe and safe SQL query patterns, not executable commands or reconnaissance behavior. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 82 starts a Markdown Python code block for an illustrative SQL injection example. It is not a shell command, Ruby execution, or executable skill logic.
Line 84 is labeled as the bad example for SQL injection education. It is documentation text inside SKILL.md, not an instruction to inspect or query a real system.
Line 87 is the safe parameterized query example paired with the unsafe example. It is documentation for review guidance, not system reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Code reviews can miss security, quality, testing, and performance problems. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a structured review with actionable findings.
actual_capabilities: Reviews code for readability, naming, complexity, and duplication.
Checks security issues including input validation, SQL injection, XSS, access control, and secret handling.
Evaluates performance risks such as inefficient queries, memory use, and caching opportunities.
Assesses test coverage, edge cases, and test quality.
Recommends documentation updates for comments, APIs, and README files.
Organizes findings by severity with practical improvement suggestions.
limitations: It depends on the code and context the user provides.
It does not run tests, compile code, or execute security scanners by itself.
It may miss issues that require production data, logs, or runtime behavior.
It provides review guidance, not formal security certification.

use_cases.title: Review a pull request
use_cases.description: Check a proposed change for correctness, maintainability, test coverage, and documentation gaps before merge.

use_cases.title: Check security risks before release
use_cases.description: Focus review attention on validation, injection, XSS, authorization, and secret handling issues.

use_cases.title: Improve legacy code maintainability
use_cases.description: Identify complex logic, duplication, unclear names, and refactoring options in existing modules.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Code Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this code for readability, bugs, and simple improvements. List the most important issues first and explain each fix.

prompt_templates.title: Pull Request Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this pull request as a teammate. Focus on correctness, maintainability, tests, and documentation. Separate blocking issues from optional improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Security-Focused Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this implementation for input validation, injection risks, authorization checks, XSS, and secret handling. Provide evidence and safer alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Deep Architecture Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this change for design tradeoffs, scalability, failure modes, testing strategy, and long-term maintainability. Identify risks, assumptions, and refactoring options.

output_examples.input: User asks for a review of a new API handler.
output: Summary: The handler is readable but needs stronger validation.
Major: Missing authorization checks could expose records to other users.
Recommendation: Add permission checks and tests for denied access.

output_examples.input: User submits a pull request for database access changes.
output: Critical: One query builds SQL from user input.
Recommendation: Use parameterized queries and add injection regression tests.
Minor: Rename a helper to clarify that it returns active users only.

output_examples.input: User requests maintainability feedback for a complex function.
output: Summary: The function mixes validation, persistence, and response formatting.
Recommendation: Extract validation and persistence into separate helpers.
Testing: Add edge case tests for missing fields and duplicate records.

best_practices: Provide the full diff, related requirements, and test results when available.
Ask for severity-ranked findings when the change is large.
Use the review feedback to update tests and documentation.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for approval based only on a small snippet of a larger change.
Do not treat suggestions as proof that code is secure.
Do not ignore project conventions when applying recommendations.

faq.question: Can this skill review any programming language?
faq.answer: It can review many languages when enough context is provided. Language-specific accuracy depends on the model and supplied code.

faq.question: Does it run code or tests?
faq.answer: No. It guides review analysis and may suggest tests, but it does not execute the project by itself.

faq.question: Is it useful for security reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks common security topics, but it is not a replacement for a formal security audit.

faq.question: How should I provide code?
faq.answer: Provide the diff, relevant files, expected behavior, and any failing tests or logs.

faq.question: Will it rewrite code for me?
faq.answer: It can propose changes and examples when requested, but the main workflow is review feedback.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
